dimension_grades.evidence: The draft contains multiple false softeners: 'even if the timing isn't right,' 'No worries if now isn't the right time,' and 'I'd love to just get 15 minutes.'
'I'd love to just get 15 minutes on your calendar to share what we're working on' states a meeting request explicitly.
The framing hedges the funding intent with 'could be a great fit' and 'for the right investor,' obscuring that this is a direct funding ask.
'I think you'd find it interesting' and 'No worries if now isn't the right time' read as strategic false-modesty tactics designed to lower resistance.
Metrics are listed with no time-based sequence or progression; there is no 'launched X months ago → now at Y' structure anywhere in the draft.
Traction data is presented as a five-item bullet list: '$1.2M ARR,' '340% YoY growth,' '47 enterprise customers,' 'NPS of 72,' 'Recently signed 3 Fortune 500 pilots.'
The isolated bullet points provide no narrative context from which a reader could extrapolate forward momentum.
No detail in the draft suggests customer pull or surprise growth; the metrics are stated flatly with no indication of how or why demand arose.

'I've been following your work at Meridian Ventures for a while now. Really impressive portfolio you've built.' references only the fund and portfolio generally, not any specific talk, post, or interview.
No thesis or stated insight of the recipient is referenced; the email only says the company 'could be a great fit for your fund' without connecting to any specific investor view.
The personalization paragraph contains only generic flattery and no metric or evidence point from the sender's business.
The flattery ('Really impressive portfolio you've built') sits as a standalone compliment entirely disconnected from the email's subsequent argument.
The draft contains 'I know you're incredibly busy,' 'Happy to work around your schedule,' and 'whenever works best for you' — all heavy deference markers.
'I'd be grateful for the opportunity to tell you more' frames the conversation as a favor to the sender, not as mutually interesting or valuable.
'Whenever works best for you' leaves scheduling entirely open-ended with no proposed time window or concrete coordination step.
Subject line 'Quick chat?' contains no traction figure, role, or domain signal of any kind.
'Quick chat?' does not indicate whether this is a funding ask, partnership inquiry, or something else entirely.
'Quick chat?' is a vague teaser designed to manufacture curiosity rather than communicate substance, functioning as a low-stakes hook trick.
